label: Peptides and oligomers
description: Peptides, nucleotides and nucleic-acid oligomers as compounds: how the chemistry step names them (sequences, repeats, cyclic peptides from one starting residue, n-mers, linkage isomers, nucleotide abbreviations, polymers of unstated length), every length of a series found in the sample papers in the compound vocabulary, and the totals: total peptide and oligomer yields and the longest oligomer of each row (uses the Solution chemistry module).
covers: peptides and nucleic-acid oligomers as compounds (each sequence or length its own column, named by the chemistry step's rules) the share of 2'-5' / 3'-5' linkages in oligomers, and their totals: total peptide yield, total oligomer yield and the longest oligomer of each row -- so no total-yield, oligomer-length or longest-product parameters.

standard_columns.description: Total yield (%) of peptides (dimers and longer, linear and cyclic): stated by the paper, else the sum of the row's peptide % yields (calculated).
Total yield (%) of nucleic-acid oligomers (2-mers and longer): stated by the paper, else the sum of the row's oligomer % yields (calculated).
Longest nucleic-acid oligomer with a value in the row (nt): stated by the paper, else from the row's oligomer columns (calculated).

chemistry: Peptides: name a peptide by its sequence in three-letter codes, N- to C-terminus, joined by "-": "Gly-Gly" (diglycine), "Gly-Gly-Gly" (triglycine), "Gly-Ala-Ala" -- order matters, so keep it exactly as the paper gives it. A run of 4 or more of one residue is written "(Gly)4": "(Gly)4" for tetraglycine, "(Gly)10", "Gly-(Ala)4". A cyclic peptide (including diketopiperazines) is "cyclo_" plus its residues the same way: "cyclo_Gly-Gly" for the glycine DKP, "cyclo_Gly-Val" (the app writes every ring from the same starting residue).

Nucleic-acid oligomers: "<n>mer_<nucleotide>" -- n the chain length, the nucleotide by its base letter, RNA "A" "C" "G" "U", DNA "dA" "dC" "dG" "dT": "4mer_A" for an adenylate tetramer / (pA)4, "43mer_U", "12mer_dT". A mixed oligomer by its letters as the paper gives them (a sequence, or a composition when the order wasn't determined): "3mer_AAU", "3mer_dATG". A table of oligomer lengths (columns 1, 2, 3, ... under "% oligomer") gives one species per length: "1mer_A", "2mer_A", ... All oligomers together (an oligomerization yield, "RNA oligomers") is named "oligomers"; the longest oligomer detected is not a species (another step records it). Polymers of unstated length: "poly(A)", "poly(dT)", "poly(Gly)".

Dinucleotides with a stated linkage keep it: "2mer_A_2'-5'" for A2'p5'A, "2mer_A_3'-5'" for A3'p5'A; with a 5'-phosphate in front, "p-2mer_A_3'-5'" for pA3'p5'A. Mononucleotides by their standard abbreviation: AMP, ADP, ATP (also for pA, ppA, pppA), dAMP, dTMP, "3'-AMP" for the 3'-phosphate, "2',3'-cAMP" and "3',5'-cAMP" for the cyclic phosphates. Never use an abbreviation that names different compounds in different papers -- 'TMP' (trimetaphosphate or thymidine monophosphate): write "trimetaphosphate" or "dTMP".

A product whose composition is known but whose SEQUENCE the paper says it didn't determine (e.g. shown in parentheses, "(FFA)") must not be given a sequence: name it by its residues and counts, e.g. "Phe2Ala (sequence not determined)".
